content: Spargel is the German term for asparagus. In Germany, most asparagus is white because it is cultivated under soil mounds to block sunlight and prevent photosynthesis. This method stops the asparagus from turning green and gives it a sweeter and more tender flavor. The harvesting season for white asparagus typically spans from late April to early June. While green asparagus is also available in Germany, it is less common and is referred to as grüner Spargel. Asparagus holds significant cultural and culinary importance in Europe, particularly in Germany, where it is often called Königliches Gemüse, meaning Royal Vegetable. Germany produces approximately 57,000 tons of asparagus annually, but this amount only satisfies 61% of the country's consumption needs. During the late spring harvest, many German cities host festivals to celebrate asparagus. For example, the city of Schwetzingen claims the title of the Asparagus Capital of the World and organizes an annual Spargelfest (asparagus festival), during which a Spargel Queen is crowned. During Spargelsaison (asparagus season), which occurs in May, asparagus is widely sold at roadside stands and open-air markets throughout Germany. It is also a highly sought-after dish in restaurants, where fresh asparagus, or frischer Spargel, is prominently advertised on menus and signs. In popular culture, the German association with asparagus is humorously referenced in the Futurama episode titled The 30% Iron Chef, where Bender's teacher is named Helmut Spargle, a nod to the German vegetable.
